1.why: All screens show a clean static layout with solid-color cards and no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings, high-contrast blue primary buttons, and focused input outlines make key actions and fields stand out clearly.

3.why: Each page is limited to one primary task with obvious labels and a single main button, allowing quick identification of the next needed action.

4.why: Users must recall a multi-part password complexity rule (14–128 chars, upper, lower, number, symbol) plus navigate many sequential token and code steps.

5.why: No password-manager prompts, autofill controls, or “remember me” options appear on any of the nine screens.

6.why: Fields start empty or show only simulation values; no visual cues for previously saved or familiar account items are present.

7.why: Labels and instructions are brief, use plain language, and remain easy to read across every step.

8.why: No error messages appear in the provided happy-path screenshots, so their quality cannot be directly verified.

9.why: The recovery page supplies an explicit format example (name@example.org or +15551234567) and password rules describe required character types.

10.why: Password and six-digit code fields are clearly labeled, yet no alternative method choices such as face login are offered.

11.why: Each screen presents only one primary action and at most a single secondary link, avoiding any choice overload.

12.why: Subsequent pages and the final confirmation explicitly state outcomes such as “recovery instructions have been prepared” and “Privacy statement accepted.”

13.why: Persistent green safe-authentication tips and short helper notes (e.g., token lifetime, logs-panel codes) appear on the relevant steps.

14.why: Fields can be re-edited and resubmitted, but no explicit “try again” controls, back links, or mistake-recovery guidance are shown.

15.why: Identical header, card layout, button styling, and green notice box are reused on every screen, keeping the design consistent.
